picks.title: A supercomputer is about to launch to the moon aboard a rover named FLIP
picks.excerpt: The FLIP lunar rover will carry the first supercomputer to the moon, bringing onboard AI processing to lunar surface operations.
picks.rationale: Space slot and the freshest item in the pool: the first supercomputer headed to the lunar surface brings onboard AI processing to rover operations.

picks.title: AI that reconstructs cloud-covered ground in satellite images with photo-like clarity
picks.excerpt: KAIST built GeoCore-9B, a 9-billion-parameter generative foundation model pretrained on 10 million satellite image-text pairs, which restores cloud-covered optical imagery and turns radar images into photo-like views, beating task-specific models.
picks.rationale: Earth-observation slot: GeoCore-9B is a new 9B-parameter foundation model that restores cloud-covered imagery and turns radar scenes into photo-like views. It is a different model from the IonQ quantum radar card published 09-28.

picks.title: Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
picks.excerpt: Google Research paired AI agents with lab robots and a digital twin (VERID) that verifies liquid-handling protocols before execution, running closed-loop campaigns on DNA aptamers and de novo protein binders that reached single-digit nanomolar binders.
picks.rationale: Lab-automation slot: agents run closed-loop wet-lab campaigns, and the VERID digital twin checks each protocol before the robot executes it. It is a new Google release, separate from the GEN hybrid digital twin card on 10-12.

picks.title: Synthetic public opinion polling: AI personas don't always change their minds like real voters do
picks.excerpt: Pollsters now use LLM-built synthetic personas as stand-ins for voters, but fixed personas miss opinion shifts and outliers; a Pew experiment found AI answers differed from human panelists by 12 points on average.
picks.rationale: Social-science methods slot: a Pew experiment measured a 12-point average gap between synthetic LLM personas and real panelists. That is a concrete limit for anyone using AI as stand-in survey respondents.

picks.title: Researchers dispute whether AI has passed the Turing test
picks.excerpt: The first experimental run of Turing's original three-player, open-ended imitation game found 36 of 37 participants correctly identified GPT-4-Turbo, challenging claims that AI has passed the Turing test.
picks.rationale: AI-cognition slot: the first run of Turing's original three-player game found that 36 of 37 people spotted the AI, which pushes back on claims that AI has passed the test.
